strips.title: The same ad, two ways — why the plan step exists

panels.head: Monday, 9 a.m.: straight to video
panels.text: One line, no plan, straight into the video model. Pretty clip, wrong colour, 25 credits gone.

panels.head: Tuesday: the plan first
panels.text: Photo in, plan out: three shots, a lens, a light, the exact colour code. Zero credits spent.

panels.head: The stills round
panels.text: Six frames for about the price of one clip. Two approved, one sent back for a wider frame.

panels.head: Wednesday: the ad
panels.text: Three clips, one retry, one voice line, one export. About 185 credits, every one of them on purpose.

strips.title: Who pays for the video — the four routes, in real life

panels.head: The bakery
panels.text: A 15-second ad for the shop down the street. The client pays per video and signs off the plan first.

panels.head: The seller
panels.text: A listing video for a product she already sells, shown exactly as it is. Amazon's video rules still apply.

panels.head: The channel
panels.text: A Shorts channel: 1,000 subscribers and 4,000 watch hours before a cent, every synthetic clip labelled.

panels.head: The reviewer
panels.text: A guide like this one. If a reader subscribes through a paid link, the tool pays a share. Disclosed above the link, every time.
